Australia (🇦🇺): Police feared Sydney street preachers with links to Islamic State would gain access to guns and tried to stop them targeting licensed owners, or “cleanskins”, years before member Naveed Akram opened fire at Bondi Beach with legally purchased weapons.

A court document also suggests ASIO questioned associates of the IS cell, but the information never reached the NSW Police tasked with approving gun licences.

The Sydney Morning Herald has also revealed an associate of the gunman planned to mimic an IS plot deployed on the same Philippines island which the alleged Bondi terrorists visited before the attack.
